recent_posts.title: Security risks of releasing AI generated code without scanning
recent_posts.summary: AI code generation tools like GitHub Copilot can introduce security risks including outdated libraries, known vulnerabilities, and license compliance issues. Organizations must not blindly release AI-generated code without automated verification. JFrog Xray enables continuous binary-level scanning across the development pipeline, while JFrog Artifactory centralizes dependency management. A three-step approach is recommended: centralize packages in Artifactory, run continuous scans with Xray, and enforce governance policies that automatically block deployments when CVSS scores exceed defined thresholds.

recent_posts.title: Accelerating AI Agent Development on Google Cloud with JFrog MCP Registry
recent_posts.summary: JFrog MCP Registry is a governance layer for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers used in agentic AI development on Google Cloud. It addresses the bottleneck between developer velocity and security review by automating policy enforcement, providing granular tool-level permissions, offering a self-serve catalog integrated with Cursor, VS Code, and Claude Code, and giving security teams full visibility into which MCP servers are active across the organization. The product is positioned as part of the JFrog AI Catalog and targets teams building Gemini-powered agents on GCP.

recent_posts.title: Building a Governed AI Model Supply Chain: Integrating AWS SageMaker and the JFrog Platform
recent_posts.summary: Integrating AWS SageMaker with JFrog Artifactory addresses the governance gap in enterprise AI model management. The post explains why S3 alone is insufficient as a model registry, highlighting issues with metadata, versioning, and fragmented audit trails across weights, inference containers, and dependencies. The proposed solution centralizes the 'Model Triad' in JFrog Artifactory, enabling immutable versioning, curated proxying for Hugging Face models, and automated SBOM/AIBOM generation via JFrog Xray. A three-stage integration walkthrough covers unified orchestration with secret externalization, secure model lineage by rerouting Hugging Face downloads through Artifactory, and dynamic runtime model resolution at inference time.

recent_posts.title: Under the Hood: Engineering JFrog Premium Availability
recent_posts.summary: JFrog details the engineering behind its 99.99% uptime SLA offering called Premium Availability. Key architectural changes include low-density 'Premium Cells' to reduce noisy-neighbor effects, graceful Kubernetes shutdown orchestration to prevent in-flight request failures, application-level resilience through priority-aware queuing and streaming-based memory management, redundant security scanning failover for Xray and related services, demand-aware autoscaling with advanced database connection pooling, and a 'last-in-line' deployment strategy that ensures only heavily validated releases reach premium customers. Proactive observability with lower alert thresholds and Sev0/1 incident escalation rounds out the offering.

recent_posts.title: JFrog launches platform skills and MCP tools for AI agents in DevSecOps workflows
recent_posts.summary: JFrog is launching official Platform Skills and expanding MCP tools to give AI coding agents full visibility into JFrog-managed software supply chains. Agents can now query artifact security data, CVEs, curation status, build provenance, and governance policies in natural language. The BYOA (Bring Your Own Agent) approach supports Cursor, Claude Code, and other coding agents via open-source skills, an MCP server, or a zero-configuration plugin. Use cases include securing pipelines, ensuring compliance, tracing build provenance, and optimizing storage costs.

recent_posts.title: Automate NIST SSDF Compliance: A Technical Guide to Policy as Code in JFrog AppTrust
recent_posts.summary: A technical guide to automating NIST SP 800-218 (SSDF) compliance using Policy as Code (PaC) with Rego inside JFrog AppTrust. Covers four concrete implementation steps: validating SBOM attestation (PS.3.2) via JFrog Xray, enforcing secure coding evidence (PW.5.1) through SonarQube integration, automating release approvals (PW.2.2) with ServiceNow change-request checks, and hardening build process security (PW.6) using GitHub provenance combined with binary-level analysis. Each step includes working Rego code snippets that can be dropped into AppTrust policies to physically block non-compliant releases from promotion.

recent_posts.title: Why AI governance requires traceability not just model safety
recent_posts.summary: AI safety and AI trust are fundamentally different things. Safety is a property of a model; trust is a property of the entire system surrounding it. Most enterprise AI governance efforts focus on model safety while ignoring traceability, ownership, and accountability across the full AI lifecycle. Shadow AI — ungoverned models entering organizations informally — compounds this problem by creating blind spots around compliance, data exposure, and supply chain risk. Closing the governance gap requires treating AI models like software artifacts: tracked provenance, automated security scans, enforced policy gates, and clear ownership at every handoff. Visibility without accountability is just noise; real trust requires embedding responsibility continuously into the AI delivery lifecycle, not bolting it on after deployment.

recent_posts.title: Recap: Women in DevSecOps Fireside Chat – Leveraging AI in Software Delivery
recent_posts.summary: A recap of JFrog's Women in DevSecOps fireside chat featuring technical leaders from Invesco and Vanguard. Key themes include AI moving from experimental to production-critical, the need for end-to-end artifact traceability, reducing developer friction by embedding security into the IDE, consolidating tools to fight sprawl, and adopting shift-left security practices. The discussion also touched on representation and mentorship for women in DevSecOps.

recent_posts.title: AI Models Won’t Pick Sides in the Security War. Governance and Policy Will.
recent_posts.summary: Two major software supply chain attacks hit LiteLLM (PyPI) and Axios (npm) within a week of each other, collectively affecting hundreds of millions of weekly downloads. The attacks exploited CI pipeline credentials and compromised maintainer accounts with sophisticated, pre-staged backdoors. Meanwhile, the median time from vulnerability disclosure to active exploitation has collapsed to near-zero, with ~70% of flaws weaponized before public disclosure. A leaked Anthropic internal document reveals a forthcoming model called 'Claude Mythos' with advanced cybersecurity capabilities, raising concerns about adversarial symmetry: the same AI that helps defenders find vulnerabilities can be used by attackers. JFrog argues that policy enforcement at the point of ingestion — governing packages, dependencies, agent skills, and MCP servers before they enter the pipeline — is the durable answer to this accelerating threat landscape.

recent_posts.title: Governance That Ships: Embedding Policy as Code Into Your System of Record
recent_posts.summary: Manual compliance processes — spreadsheets, screenshots, attestations — create an 'Audit Tax' that doesn't scale with modern AI-accelerated development. Policy as Code (PaC) using Open Policy Agent (OPA) and Rego translates governance rules into machine-readable, automatically enforced logic. However, homegrown OPA scripts in CI pipelines have critical flaws: point-in-time validation, visibility gaps when pipelines are bypassed, fragmented metadata, and high operational burden. JFrog AppTrust addresses this by embedding native PaC enforcement directly into the artifact repository (JFrog Artifactory), offering a 'Bring Your Own Policy' model that accepts existing OPA/Rego rules. This approach cryptographically binds compliance evidence to binaries, centralizes attestations, and provides machine-speed proof required by regulations like the EU Cyber Resilience Act and NIST SSDF.
